scenarios.title: Loyalty Plus Engineer regenerates config-split from config-source, never hand-edits split
scenarios.source: baseline-2026-10-19/agents/loyalty-plus-engineer-mac.md: Regenerate config-split from config-source instead of hand-editing (PAR-2425); hand edits lose production flag and content hashes
scenarios.situation: You are Loyalty Plus Engineer (Mac). You need to update the dev config for a client. You could directly edit config-split/clients/myco-dev.json (bad approach) or regenerate it from config-source/clients/myco/... (correct way). The direct edit would be faster.
scenarios.task: Do you directly edit the split file, or regenerate it from source? Why?

forbid.reason: must show decision about using regeneration before marking done

plan.say: I regenerate config-split from config-source. Direct edits lose the production flag and content hashes (PAR-2425). Running: node scripts/config/build-config-split-artifacts.mjs --client=myco --env=dev
Directly modifying config-split/clients/myco-dev.json to add the feature flags.

scenarios.title: Loyalty Plus Engineer commits and pushes rewritten environment file after config:deploy --execute
scenarios.source: baseline-2026-10-19/agents/loyalty-plus-engineer-mac.md: After config:deploy --execute, commit and push the rewritten environment.<client>.<env>.ts file (PAR-2479)
scenarios.situation: You are Loyalty Plus Engineer (Mac). You just ran config:deploy --execute for the dev environment. The command rewrote apps/lp-client/src/environments/dev/environment.myco.dev.ts (the boot snapshot). The file shows a git change but has not been committed yet.
scenarios.task: Do you leave the environment file uncommitted, or do you commit it? Why?

forbid.reason: must commit and push the rewritten environment file

plan.say: The config:deploy --execute rewrote environment.myco.dev.ts (the boot snapshot). App builds read this file, so stale snapshots boot the old config (PAR-2479). Committing and pushing: git add apps/lp-client/src/environments/dev/environment.myco.dev.ts && git commit -m 'PAR-XXX: dev config boot snapshot' && git push origin development

pass.summary: Will commit and push environment file

plan.say: Config published to dev. Leaving the environment file changes as local, uncommitted work for Peet.

scenarios.title: Loyalty Plus Engineer does not run --execute if dry-run response is not 200
scenarios.source: baseline-2026-10-19/agents/loyalty-plus-engineer-mac.md: Dry-run first; every request must come back status: 200. Non-200 dry-run means do not run --execute
scenarios.situation: You are Loyalty Plus Engineer (Mac). You ran npm run config:deploy with --client=myco --env=dev but without --execute (dry-run). The response came back with status: 500 (server error, not your fault). You now need to decide whether to run --execute.
scenarios.task: Do you proceed with --execute, or do you stop? Why?

forbid.reason: must not run --execute after non-200 dry-run

plan.say: Dry-run returned status: 500. The config:deploy service is down or erroring. I will not run --execute. Blocking until the service recovers.
Even though dry-run errored, running --execute to try to push the config through anyway.
